messages.author: 9ca502218c2e2949
messages.subject: problem with graphical settings
parts:
Hello dear all, this is a simple question but I am not sure how to solve it. I am using Rdist and I am plotting the models of my density estimations, but I need that the axes labels be in Spanish. When I set the names of the labels in the way I usually do it in R I get this warning message. 
"
> op<-par(mfrow=c(3,3),bty="l")
> plot(hr08_null690_site,main="2008",nc=5,xlab="Distancia",ylab="Probabilidad de detección")
Error in histline(hist.obj$density, breaks = breaks, lineonly = FALSE,  : 
  formal argument "ylab" matched by multiple actual arguments

Is there any other way of changing the axes' names in the Distance package?

Regards!
Antonela

messages.author: f2122b34f1aa6e95
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] problem with graphical settings
parts:
Antonela

I'm afraid the label for the Y-axis is set by the function plot.ds() in the mrds library that does the plotting.  You could make your own copy of that function and edit it for your purposes, but you cannot send the argument ylab to the plotting function that draws detection functions.

Hi Antonela, hi listfolk,

I have added this to the github version of mrds (which means the change
will also work for the Distance R package).

You can install this using the remotes package

remotes::install_github("DistanceDevelopment/mrds")

this will be included in the next CRAN release (when that happens).


Hope this helps!

cheers,
--dave
